A leading independent day school for girls & boys 3 - 18
Welcome
At Churcher's College we seek to maximise the potential of every one of our pupils. We aim to achieve that within a happy, caring, and well-structured environment.
Dive into a world of opportunities for growth and discovery, where academic excellence, athletic achievement, award-winning arts and boundless adventures converge to offer our pupils unparalleled experiences for growth and discovery.
At the heart of everything we do
Pastoral care
Happy, confident children thrive. Our warm, welcoming and nurturing environment ensures that every pupil feels valued and supported, enabling them to succeed academically and in the many extra-curricular activities on offer. We encourage a culture of openness and are committed to providing continuity of pastoral care throughout a pupil’s time at Churcher’s.
From the magic and discovery of Nursery and Junior School to the inspiration and adventure of Senior and Sixth Form, life at Churcher’s is full of opportunity, learning and happiness.
A snapshot of school life

Performing Arts
Performing Arts plays a vibrant role in life at school. On any given day at Churcher’s, the distant sound of an orchestra rehearsing, an instrument being perfected, or lines being practiced can be caught in the air.
Young people join us brimming with possibilities, eager to discover and cultivate their abilities. We offer a vast array of opportunities for them to explore, develop and channel where their passions may lead.
Participation in performing arts activities also builds transferable skills like collaboration, resilience, and self-confidence, which are invaluable for students' personal and professional futures
There is a vast and varied landscape of possibilities for pupils of all abilities to get involved from performances on stage to behind-the-scenes magic, as well as many supra-curricular and extra-curricular activities.
Music
Music is embedded in the fabric of school culture and community. Whether it is simply for pleasure, or a career ambition, music plays an integral part in the education of all our pupils, from the First Year through to Sixth Form. Supporting the students is a large team of music staff, including 29 peripatetic instrument teachers, enabling this thriving department to flourish and deliver a comprehensive offering.
Drama
At Churcher’s we embrace the philosophy that the arts can enrich and change lives. Drama is a thriving department at Churcher’s College, filled with fun, laughter and enjoyment. Offering a unique form of creative expression, drama provides students with unlimited benefits - building confidence, empathy, communication skills, teamwork and collaboration, to name but a few. These are essential, transferable skills for everyday life at school and beyond.

An Opportunity to Visit Us
Come and see what makes our Senior School & Sixth Form so special.
We’d be delighted to welcome you to one of our open events, usually held during the school day, where you can explore our facilities and meet our students and teachers, getting a real feel for life at Churcher’s.
To book a place, simply choose the event you’d like to attend from the list below. Personal tours are also available and can be arranged at the bottom of this page. You can also get in touch with our Admissions team by email or on 01730 236825 to arrange a visit on a day that suits you. We very much look forward to meeting you.
Book onto an Open Event
Our open events offer an opportunity to come in person and visit us during the school day. Your visit will start with a welcome talk by the Headmaster, followed by a tour of the school in small groups with one of our Sixth Form pupils. Children are also very welcome.
Personal Tours
We are happy to offer individual or family tours to give our visitors an additional opportunity to explore our school, led by our Sixth Form students. Places are limited and booking is essential. Please click below to reserve your space.

Pastoral Care
Pastoral care is at the heart of all we do. The pastoral care system at Churcher’s begins with an underlying ethos of consideration and kindness.
Our welcoming, nurturing and secure environment ensures that every pupil feels valued and supported, enabling them to succeed academically, and in the many extra-curricular activities on offer. We encourage a culture of openness and are committed to providing continuity of pastoral care throughout a pupil’s time at Churcher’s. Our pastoral system is one based upon open communication between pupils and staff. Our pupils have a host of adults in the school community to whom they can talk, and who will have concern and compassion for them.
Open communication
The relationship with a pupil’s Head of House and Form Tutor is a particularly important one. However, some pupils will find they talk most easily to one of our School Nurses, or one of their subject teachers. Some students prefer to talk to our dedicated School Counsellor, or our school Chaplain, if they are worried about something specific because they find these specialist members of staff particularly accessible and reassuring.
In essence, we believe that it would be hard for a Churcher’s pupil not to find someone to whom they find it easy to talk.
A key feature of our pastoral provision is a strong partnership between school and home. Open dialogue with parents is actively encouraged and contributes significantly to maintaining the happiness and wellbeing of our pupils.
Perhaps most importantly, Churcher’s pupils also share problems with each other, and are incredibly supportive, tolerant and understanding of their peers; we see this as one of the defining characteristics of our school.
The House System
The House system provides every Churcher’s student with a consistent pastoral relationship throughout school. Forming a core part of the school pastoral system, Heads of House and their teams foster relationships and understanding with each pupil in their care to deliver the support and guidance needed for a happy and healthy school experience.
Sixth Form Pastoral Care
Our aim is to ensure Churcher’s Sixth Form students find the school to be a nurturing and supportive environment where they can develop and thrive. Sixth Form is a time of great challenge and opportunity, so we focus on working in partnership with parents to help our pupils flourish.
We have a dedicated team of staff members to support our students. Key figures with specific responsibility for student welfare in Sixth Form include the Head of Sixth Form, Deputy Head of Sixth Form Pastoral and the five Heads of House.
We are proud that our busy and vibrant Sixth Form is small enough for students to be known personally, for their potential to be recognised and developed, and individual support given where needed. There are certainly many opportunities for pupils to get involved with at Churcher’s, and our dedicated team of staff members are here to support them on their journey.
Tutors and support
Significant additional support in Sixth Form comes in the form of a Personal Tutor whose role is to oversee all academic and pastoral matters for the individuals in their care. Personal Tutors will meet and talk regularly with their tutees about all aspects of Sixth Form life, helping students achieve the optimum work life balance as they navigate the challenges of A Levels and preparation for life beyond school. We recognise the importance of strong links between school and home, and the Personal Tutor is the first point of liaison with parents.
Form Tutors, wellbeing and medical staff also play a significant role in supporting our students through their time in the Sixth Form. We have a dedicated School Counsellor, Special Educational Needs Co-Ordinator and a School Nurse permanently on-site taking care of the welfare of pupils.
PSHE and Life Skills
Our Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) for Sixth Form includes life skills, leadership training, team building and guest speakers, and complements the stimulating enrichment programme and work done on higher education, university preparation and future careers.
We aim to help students to become responsible and capable members of wider society and encourage them to lead healthy lifestyles. The Sixth Form pastoral programme includes a series of helpful talks and seminars about learning to cope with stress, resilience, exam planning and mindfulness. We also weave in initiatives from the Local Health Authority and Hampshire Police, plus the ‘Safe Drive Stay Alive’ seminar which coincides with the age when many students learn to drive.
We also offer 'Spiritual Spaces', a set of reflection themes that Form Tutors discuss weekly with students during tutorial time. These sessions enable students to pause, reflect, consider, and discuss issues which may be topical, moral, or ethical such as forgiveness, cyber security, and the role of free speech.

Sport
Churcher’s enjoys a strong sporting tradition and reputation, understanding the power of sport in developing individuals as well as bringing our whole community together.
Sport gives our pupils the chance for both achievement and opportunity. We champion all pupils, recognising not only sporting excellence but also progress and endeavour - our aim is to provide every pupil with positive sporting experiences. We strive to develop good character, teamwork skills, leadership opportunities and a life-long appreciation of physical activity.
Weekly Sport
Senior School pupils take part in a double PE lesson and a double Games lesson every week. The PE lesson curriculum is designed to help pupils find their sporting 'niche' through exposure to a variety of physical activities and sports, improving fitness and physical literacy. Games lessons are centred on our Major Sport Programme, teaching skill development in specific sports and providing positive competitive experiences. We are proud of our high participation rates across all year groups in our Saturday fixtures programme.
Autumn: Rugby & Hockey Spring: Hockey & Netball Summer: Cricket

ISI Inspection Reports & Reviews
In accordance with best practice and statutory regulations, Churcher’s College undergoes regular inspections. The purposes of inspection are to ensure that standards are maintained and that schools comply with the relevant legal requirements.
Latest Inspection Reports
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) is an independent, government-approved body which provides objective inspections to safeguard the quality and effectiveness of the education, care and welfare of children in schools. The ISI is not an arm of the government, but an independent, not-for-profit inspectorate. The most recent Churcher's ISI inspection report available is from December 2025.
We recommend you click the boxes below to read the last few ISI reports and reviews from other noteworthy sources.
The quality of the pupils’ personal development... academic and other activities is excellent.
You’ll find every opportunity you could hope for here at Churcher’s, the huge offering in adventure, sport and the arts providing an excellent ballast to all that hard work. Indeed, parents reckon they’ve hit gold.
Good Schools Guide 2023

Outdoor Learning & Adventure
Nurturing an adventurous spirit is a core value at Churcher’s. Taking lessons outside and offering plenty of opportunities to explore has many benefits for learning and development; plus it is great fun too!
At Churcher's, we take a rounded view of your child's education, using our fantastic facilities and acres of space to enhance their school experience. By weaving outdoor learning into the school day, we help children deepen their understanding of subjects while encouraging their happiness, health, and creativity to flourish.
Outdoor Learning
Learning outside the classroom is embedded throughout the curriculum. Taking our learning outdoors promotes:
Creativity and artistic expression
Teamwork and relationship-building
Environmentally aware individuals
Academic and social skills
A Through-School Approach
Our youngest children delight in the wonders of gardening, sensory play, and exploring the beauty of nature. These activities spark curiosity and joy, laying the foundation for a lifelong love of learning. As pupils grow, outdoor adventures continue with playful bug hunts, imaginative storytelling, and hands-on experiences that bring lessons to life.
As children progress, outdoor learning remains a cherished part of their journey. Whether sharing stories in our Outdoor Classroom, creating scale models of the solar system on the school field, or measuring distance for maths, we embrace every opportunity to take learning beyond the classroom. deepening understanding, and make education an exciting adventure for every child.
Adventurous Activities
In the Junior School, we provide challenging and adventurous activities that provide the opportunity for children to take risks in a controlled environment. Activities in school may include campfire events in our Outdoor Classroom and Firepit, or teambuilding sessions on our onsite Low Ropes course.
Children also relish the chance to attend residential trips off-site and days out, helping them build confidence and self-esteem. Activities including archery, quad biking, paddleboarding and more, providing exciting opportunities for personal growth and skill development.
Our Facilities
Our beautiful school grounds offer plenty of opportunities for outdoor learning, adventure and exploration.
Sensory garden
Outdoor learning area and campfire
School pond
Large field
Greenhouse and gardening area
Trim trail

Adventure
Adventure is a beloved feature of life at Churcher’s College which contributes to an education that nurtures the whole person.
The adventurous activities programme enables students to venture outside the traditional learning environment and get stuck into and learn about the great outdoors, both in the UK and overseas. We actively encourage students to broaden their horizons and develop skills for life by taking risks outside of their comfort zone. Our aim is for pupils to develop into well-rounded, self-confident, and socially aware individuals.
The Adventurous Activities Journey
Our idyllic location in the South Downs National Park, just a stone's throw from the south coast, offers pupils the chance to immerse themselves in the great outdoors from the start. Students are given progressively larger opportunities and expeditions as they move further up the school, using the ever-growing experiences gained. We travel across the UK, including the Brecon Beacons, to Dartmoor, the Lake District and the Highlands of Scotland - and beyond, to Norway, Peru and Bolivia, Romania, eSwatini and more - to offer new challenges in inspiring environments. Alongside regular off-site trips, all facilities at Churcher’s are also utilised, including our indoor 25-metre swimming pool, climbing wall and extensive green spaces.
The Adventure Team
The programme is headed up by our dedicated Head of Adventure and a team of professional and experienced staff with relevant and appropriate qualifications. This also includes external professionals and parent volunteers, drawing on a large pool of experience and connections, which enables us to offer such an expansive range of activities.

Creative Excellence
Churcher’s College firmly embraces the philosophy that every student is an artist. The creative arts are held in high esteem at Churcher’s. We offer outstanding resources to encourage artistic exploration and expression.
Whether in the form of fine art canvases, beautifully crafted furniture, computer-aided design, or precision engineering – we encourage our pupils to explore and expand their creative talents.We offer students a rich curriculum of creative subjects at GCSE and A level, designed to inspire, challenge and develop exceptional talent. Visitors consistently comment on the outstanding quality of the work produced by our students and there are always displays in the studios as well as major pieces of work around the school buildings, reinforcing Churcher's Art Dept as a place where students achieve outstanding results.
Art & Design
Our Art & Design Department at Churcher’s is a vibrant and industrious hive of creativity. Students are given the opportunity to use a variety of media including drawing, painting, 3D, photography, pottery and mixed-media.
Students opting to study Art & Design at GCSE and at A level are encouraged to think creatively. We focus on teaching practical skills to a very high level. Alongside, students gain a deeper understanding of Art & Design through exploring the work of a rich mix of historic and contemporary artists.
At exam level the work produced is consistently of an exceptionally high standard. The courses are Fine Art based with the emphasis on encouraging students to work independently but from an informed background, and to develop skills and understanding through challenging projects set by the Art Department staff.
Design Technology
Design and Technology (D&T) provides students with the opportunity to combine creative flair with practical skills.
Our state-of-the-art D&T department is fully equipped with a Computer Aided Design (CAD) studio, laser cutters, lathes, an overhead router, a design library and research area and digital photography and scanning equipment.
The Art Department at Churcher's nurtures confident, curious thinkers and makers.
Tim Strange, Head of Art

An Opportunity to Visit Us
Come and see what makes our Senior School & Sixth Form so special.
We’d be delighted to welcome you to one of our open events, usually held during the school day, where you can explore our facilities and meet our students and teachers, getting a real feel for life at Churcher’s.
To book a place, simply choose the event you’d like to attend from the list below. Personal tours are also available and can be arranged at the bottom of this page. You can also get in touch with our Admissions team by email or on 01730 236825 to arrange a visit on a day that suits you. We very much look forward to meeting you.
Book onto an Open Event
Our open events offer an opportunity to come in person and visit us during the school day. Your visit will start with a welcome talk by the Headmaster, followed by a tour of the school in small groups with one of our Sixth Form pupils. Children are also very welcome.
Personal Tours
We are happy to offer individual or family tours to give our visitors an additional opportunity to explore our school, led by our Sixth Form students. Places are limited and booking is essential. Please click below to reserve your space.

Academic Excellence
At Churcher’s pupils thrive in an atmosphere of high expectation and achievement.
We have a long history of examination and university success, and pupils are taught in an environment which is stimulating, challenging and engaging.
The College strives for academic excellence and provides pupils with the skills they need to successfully question, debate and discover both in the classroom and during independent learning. We are keen to develop thinkers who can tackle life’s challenges and solve them.
Churcher’s Ranking in Sunday Times Parent Power
Value-Added
Independent analysis from Cambridge University shows that Churcher's College adds considerable value, well above the national average, to the student's academic outcome when compared with similar independent schools nationwide. The results of this research are published annually and Churcher’s College has consistently performed at an exceptional level since 2010.
Percentage of results awarded grade A and above in all subjects combined by centre type between 2018 & 2024.
(Data from Gov.uk - Guide to AS and A Level Results England, Summer 2024)
ALIS - A Level Value-Added
Comparison of Churcher’s College overall A Level value-added with schools/colleges nationally.
The background area is a normal distribution graph representing the distribution of the average value-added (standardised residual) scores for all schools/college in ALIS. The solid blue line is the value-added score for Churcher’s College.
Secondary: School Value-Added
Exam Year: 2025 | Show: National Standardisation | Year of Assessment: 2023 - 2024: Year 10 | Qualification: GCSE (9-1) | Subject(s): (multiple values) | Gender(s): All
Learning Support
In addition to more formal channels of academic support, most departments offer pupils drop-in support sessions with specific focus on understanding specification content and exam technique. These sessions provide pupils with the opportunity to receive individual attention to address any issues or problem areas that they may have encountered during lessons and to receive further support and guidance. As the pupils progress through the school we aim to gradually give them more responsibility for their learning so they leave us with the necessary skills for success at university and beyond.
Special Educational Needs
Churcher’s is proud to provide exemplary support for SEND pupils. Our Head of Curriculum Support, Ruth Saunders, leads a team of four who specialise in helping pupils to maximise their potential by overcoming any educational difficulties they may encounter, whether they be in the classroom, in exams, at home, or anywhere else. Pupils can feel confident that the Churcher’s Curriculum Support Department will ensure that their abilities are developed to their full potential, allowing them to enjoy their studies fully and maximise success in examinations.
Pupils display high levels of knowledge, skills and understanding in all subjects.
